Thanks for sending the draft DPA yesterday. Procurement ran the redline past our data protection team overnight and they flagged two categories we need to resolve before legal can approve: (1) controller/processor role table — Acadia needs a clearer statement about processor sub-delegation (we want an explicit list of allowed subprocessors and a notification timeline); and (2) cross-border transfers — we prefer standard SCCs but want an explicit fallback if Redwood updates model hosting regions (how will transfers be communicated and audited).

I attached our annotated copy for context (file: Acadia_DPA_comments_v2.pdf). Can you confirm which Redwood contacts will be accountable for the subprocessor inventory/evidence and a timeline for shipping requested artifacts (SOC2 scope, orderform mapping)?

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Josh Smith <josh.smith@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and SCCs — initial ask

Team / Josh —

Thanks for the context and Ben for the draft. High-level legal view after quick pass:
1) Subprocessor delegation: we can accept an "approved categories" approach for certain infra providers (CDN, monitoring) but Acadia's ask for an explicit pre-approved list will require a different operating model. Proposal: accept a near-term list of critical subprocessors (we'll enumerate), and commit to 30-day notice + option for Acadia to object to new critical-category subprocessors with escalation to a privacy officer. This preserves operational agility while giving Acadia control over sensitive categories.

2) SCCs / fallback: rather than baking a free-form fallback clause, we propose: (a) include current EU SCCs template as the primary transfer mechanism; (b) add a clause that if we change hosting regions in a way that materially affects transfers, Redwood will notify and provide updated SCCs or equivalent safeguards within 14 days and offer documented migration options or Order Form amendments where necessary. That satisfies auditability and gives Acadia a remediation path.

3) Evidence & timelines: I can commit to delivering a SOC2 scope statement and the subprocessor inventory extract by Thursday EOD (I'll redact internal IPs). Ben: please confirm whether the orderform will include a pinned-region checkbox for Acadia or if they will remain unpinned.

Josh — please confirm if the proposed delegation approach is acceptable. If yes, we'll prepare a clean redline and a tracked-redline set for signature.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: legal_summary_subprocessors.txt]
